thread:
Alex: Heads-up — noticed a p99 token latency surge correlated with KV evictions under sustained long-context workloads. Numbers jump from ~18ms -> ~95ms for token generation when background paging starts.

Mira: I saw that in canary last night, same pattern. p50 unchanged but p99 spikes and tail is noisy. Logs show lots of `evict_candidate` churn. :frowning:

Alex: repro trace attached from local perf harness: massive number of small evict/reinsert ops during a single long chat session. Seems to line up with FIFO/LRU comparator path.

Jorge: Quick profiling dump (flame samples): eviction handler holds pager lock and serializes token emit path for ~40-60ms bursts. Flame link: https://internal.flames/redwood/kv-evict-1742 (public link redacted).

Priya: Might be the sampling window we added last quarter. Under pressure we increase candidates and then reinsert them rapidly, causing fragmentation and extra pointer churn.

Alex: Repro steps I used:
```
# small harness to reproduce on devbox
./kv_bench --mode=chat --context-len=64k --concurrency=12 --kv-pressure=heavy --evict-policy=lru
```
Observed stable repro in ~45s. If I switch evict-policy to fifo the tails are slightly better but correctness regressions pop up (stale-kv hits).

Mira: Can you paste the exact metric names you saw? I want to correlate with observability.

Alex: Sure: kv.evictions.count, kv.evictions.reinserts, kv.pager.latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), runtime.token_emit.latency_ms.p99. Evictions/reinserts spike right before token_emit p99 jump.

Jorge: I ran a differential with commits and saw a regression after commit abc1234 (kernel selection tweak + batching heuristics). The batching change reduced throughput slightly but exposed eviction window timing.

Priya: Interesting — kernel selection lowered per-token CPU so the eviction loop has higher relative occupancy and now competes more for the pager lock. We should look at moving eviction into background thread pool or make reinserts lock-free.

Mira: Quick experiment idea: add a tiny backoff when reinserting to reduce reinsert storms. Example patch:
```
// pseudo
if (reinsert_count > 8) { sleep_us(50); }
```
This lowered p99 from 95ms -> 48ms in my dev runs (non-ideal but promising).

Alex: Good signal. Also saw fragmentation grow over long contexts — allocator churn visible in jemalloc stats. Maybe batching of reinserts into a compact pass will help.

Jorge: Created repro job and attached perf traces to ticket: https://rwd/tickets/INF-4821. I'll add flame snapshots and the AB test artifacts.

Priya: For correctness, we need a small fuzz test to ensure FIFO fallback doesn't return stale KV for pinned session contexts. I'll add an invariant check in the KV read path.

ci-bot: Build 2025.4.1742010 passed for branch kv-evict-mitigations.

Alex: Plan for next steps: 1) Add reinsertion micro-backoff, 2) deferred compact pass under pressure, 3) add fuzz invariant for FIFO fallback, 4) run 24h stress on canary. I'll open a PR with bench numbers.

Mira: Thanks — assign me to canary run and I'll collect end-to-end traces. :thumbsup:

Priya: Also add telemetry: sample reinsert bursts and snapshot fragmentation percentage every minute so we can graph correlation.

Jorge: I'll draft the postmortem if this reproduces in prod. For now, let's keep the FIFO/LRU comparison notes in the ticket and avoid rolling back kernel changes unless canary fails badly.

Alex: All right. Filing follow-ups in INF-4821 and INF-4830. Thanks everyone.
